quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: In a group ride, where should inexperienced riders position themselves?

options.text: Just behind the leader.
In front of the group.
At the rear of the group.
Beside the leader.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders behind them watch them and help if needed.

questions.question: What is a benefit of a shatter-resistant face shield?

options.text: It can protect your face in a crash.
It only protects riders from dirt.
It does not protect as well as goggles.
It should not be used with a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can protect your face in a crash.
questions.explanation: A shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A face shield also shields you from dirt, dust, insects, rain, and small rocks.

questions.question: What should your lane position help you do?

options.text: Show other drivers what you plan to do.
Stop other drivers from passing you.
Get to your destination as fast as possible.
Stay hidden in other drivers' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: A good lane position shows other drivers your intentions and keeps them from trying to share your lane.

questions.question: What should your lane position do?

options.text: Keep other drivers from sharing your lane.
Give you a good view of scenery.
Put you in other drivers' blind spots.
Hide what you plan to do from other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep other drivers from sharing your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position keeps you out of blind spots, helps you see and be seen, avoids road hazards, avoids wind blasts, and gives you an escape route. Position yourself so other drivers will not try to share your lane.

questions.question: What must you do when passing another vehicle?

options.text: You can finish the pass in a no passing zone.
You can go 10 mph over the speed limit to pass.
You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
You must complete the pass on the road shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish the pass in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: Passing must be done only in areas where it is safe and legal. You must start and complete the pass within the speed limit in a passing zone.

questions.question: Why should you use your mirrors when stopped at an intersection?

options.text: To see if parked vehicles are entering traffic.
To watch for vehicles changing lanes.
To check for vehicles coming up behind you that may not stop.
To see if vehicles behind you plan to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: To check for vehicles coming up behind you that may not stop.
questions.explanation: Use your mirrors at intersections to watch for vehicles approaching from behind. Drivers may not see you until they are very close, so you need to be ready to react.

questions.question: What does eye contact with a driver mean?

options.text: They see you.
It will never happen.
It does not mean they will yield to you.
It guarantees they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not trust eye contact to guarantee a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but do not consciously notice them.

questions.question: What happens if your front tire goes flat while riding?

options.text: The steering will feel heavy.
The steering will feel loose.
The steering will feel normal.
The ride will feel smoother.

questions.correctAnswerText: The steering will feel heavy.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes steering feel heavy. If you notice heavy steering, leave the road right away and check your tires.

questions.question: What should you do before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time?

options.text: Read books about carrying passengers.
Practice on a quiet road.
Flash your lights so others see you.
Practice on the road shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice on a quiet road.
questions.explanation: Before riding with a passenger in traffic, practice on a quiet road. This helps you get used to how your motorcycle handles with the extra weight.

questions.question: How often should you check your motorcycle's hydraulic fluid at minimum?

options.text: Once a day
Once a week
Once a year
Before every ride

questions.correctAnswerText: Once a week
questions.explanation: Check your hydraulic fluids and coolants at least once a week. Regular inspections help keep your motorcycle safe.

questions.question: What about the front brake?

options.text: Use it only when you need to stop quickly.
Use it only on slippery roads.
It is not as strong as the rear brake.
It is safe to use if you use it correctly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is safe to use if you use it correctly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop. The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It is safe to use if you use it correctly.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a good way to be more visible to other drivers?

options.text: Wearing proper clothing
Using your headlight all the time
Using your turn signals
Waving at other drivers

questions.correctAnswerText: Waving at other drivers
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright clothing with reflective material, use your headlight all the time, and use your signals and brake lights correctly. Waving at drivers is not an effective safety measure.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift lever?

options.text: In front of the left footrest
In front of the right footrest
On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: When stopping, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the rear brake first.
Apply the front brake first.
Apply both brakes at the same time.
Use only one brake, front or rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Apply them at the same time.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume motorcycles are as easy to see as other vehicles.
Assume other drivers cannot see you.
Not worry about whether other drivers see you.
Ride aggressively.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume other drivers cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and have fewer and smaller lights than other vehicles. They are hard to see. For safety, ride defensively and assume that other drivers do not see you.

questions.question: To lean a motorcycle when turning, what should you do?

options.text: Always press the left handgrip.
Always press the right handgrip.
Press the handgrip opposite the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. To make it lean, press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.

questions.question: At night, how should your following distance compare to daytime?

options.text: Allow more following distance at night.
Allow less following distance at night.
Keep the same following distance day and night.
Following distance does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow more following distance at night.
questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distances in the dark because you cannot see shadows or light contrasts. Allow a longer following distance at night than during the day.

questions.question: To stop quickly, what is best?

options.text: Release the throttle and use the front brake.
Use the rear brake only.
Use the front brake only.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
How fast a person drinks
Body weight
Height

questions.correctAnswerText: Height
questions.explanation: BAC is affected by the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast a person drinks, and body weight. Height does not affect BAC.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When it starts raining, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Do not ride down the center of a lane in wet weather. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left tire track is often best, but this depends on traffic and other conditions.

questions.question: What should NOT be included in your pre-ride inspection?

options.text: A tire check.
A taillight test.
A headlight test.
A paint check.

questions.correctAnswerText: A paint check.
questions.explanation: Check your tires, oil, fluids, lights, signals, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn before every ride. Do a complete pre-ride inspection each time you ride.

questions.question: How should a group ride when entering a curve?

options.text: Ride in a single-file formation.
Ride in a staggered formation.
Ride in pairs.
Ride on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is usually best. However, switch to single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: If you wait one hour after drinking one alcoholic drink, what is true?

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and driving.
Alcohol will not affect your riding skills.
Alcohol effects may still be present.
You will be fine if you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol effects may still be present.
questions.explanation: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can still build up in your system even at this rate. This buildup can affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: What is the best sitting position for riding?

options.text: Your arms hold you up.
You can easily reach the controls.
Your arms are straight when holding the grips.
Your knees stay away from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can easily reach the controls.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up. Do not stretch to reach the handgrips. Your arms should be slightly bent. Keep your knees against the gas tank to stay balanced.
